subject: Follow-up: integration checklist + intermittent 5xx on embeddings/reranker

Subject: Follow-up: integration checklist + intermittent 5xx on embeddings/reranker

Hi Ian — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we can get your integration stable before test traffic next week:

Summary of what we discussed:
- Goal: enable Atlas Payments to use Redwood embeddings + reranker to prioritize fraud signals in real time.
- Symptom you reported: occasional 5xx errors during batch reranker requests; appears ~1 in 300 requests during spikes.
- Short-term priority: reproduce and stabilize; medium-term: tune batch sizing and caching to reduce cost/latency.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Priyom (me): run a focused triage session with your engineers and our oncall (Ben) — proposing Fri Apr 16 10am PT.
- Ian / Atlas: share a minimal request + SDK logs (we asked for SDK logs and a sample payload) — you mentioned you can produce a snippet of the failing payloads.
- Ben (Redwood SE): initial hypothesis is token-refresh + routing mismatch causing a small window of 5xxs — Ben will outline repro steps.

Attached: postcall-checklist.pdf (high level validation steps we’ll run in the triage session).

For the triage session I want to ask you to have one engineer with access to the service logs and the SDK runtime ready. If possible include the SDK version and environment (node/python, containerization).

Thanks — I’ll send calendar invite after you confirm Fri 10am PT works.

—
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up: integration checklist + intermittent 5xx on embeddings/reranker

Thanks Priyom — Fri works. Added a quick log snippet and a sample failing payload.

Observed behavior:
- SDK: redwood-sdk-js@0.9.4 running in Node 18 on Kubernetes (EKS).
- Spike pattern: after ~180-220 requests within a minute we start to see 503 / 5xx responses from the reranker endpoint. Not every run, highly intermittent.
- Error observed in logs: "503 Service Unavailable - upstream timeout" followed by a short burst of retries.

Sample failing request (redacted):
POST /v1/rerank
{
  \"model\": \"redwood/reranker-latest\",
  \"queries\": [\"txn_12345...\"],
  \"documents\": [ ... 25 docs ... ],
  \"structured_output\": true
}

Attached: sdk-log-snippet.txt (contains timestamps and the SDK stack trace around the 503s).

We can join Fri but pinging Ben if there are any quick flags we should flip ahead of time.

—
Ian Walker
Engineering Manager, Atlas Payments
ian.walker@atlas-pay.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ian Walker <ian.walker@atlas-pay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-14T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: integration checklist + intermittent 5xx on embeddings/reranker

Ian — thanks for the snippet, that helps. Quick triage notes and a targeted checklist to speed the Friday session.

Initial hypotheses (from runtime patterns we see in similar cases):
1) Token refresh loop: if the client SDK tries to refresh an expiring token while a hot batch is being routed, downstream services can briefly return 5xxs; pattern: 401 then 5xx.
2) Structured_output path: the structured output / tool-calling path exercises extra kernels and streaming code — there have been rare regressions when a request includes both structured output + very large doc sets.
3) Backend batching threshold: a burst that crosses a batching boundary can overload a particular GPU instance if cache misses accumulate.

Quick checks before the call (low cost):
- Confirm SDK version exactly (npm list redwood-sdk-js). We’ve seen regressions before 0.10.x but unlikely in 0.9.4 — still helpful.
- Turn on DEBUG on the SDK process (REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1) to capture token-refresh events.
- For an immediate workaround: set structured_output: false for a subset of requests, or reduce per-request docs to 8–12.
- Increase client-side timeout to 60s (from default 30s) while we bisect.

Minimal repro steps for us to run in the triage session (what I’ll ask you to run):
1) Run a synthetic load (200 RPS sustained for 60s) using your production request shape.
2) Run again with structured_output=false.
3) Run again with explicit short-lived token to see if we can trigger refresh path.

Can you paste a minimal curl (we prefer a curl sample) that reproduces the request shape? If not, we can script one on the call.

Thanks — I’ll join Fri and bring a runtime engineer.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-15T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: integration checklist + intermittent 5xx on embeddings/reranker

Thanks Ian — confirming Friday Apr 16 10:00am PT (invite sent). A couple of immediate items so our time is productive:

1) Temporary workaround to apply now (non-disruptive):
- Pin the model field to redwood/reranker-v2 (avoid rolling latest)
- On the client, set max_tokens: 256 and timeout_ms: 60000
- If possible, set structured_output: false for 10% of reranker traffic to observe if the error rate drops immediately

2) Token refresh guard (short-term):
- If your token expiry window is <= 30s, refresh proactively when remaining_lifetime < 5s. That prevents in-flight refresh races. Ben will share a small snippet on the call.

3) What to bring to the session:
- The sdk-log-snippet.txt you attached (good). Also bring kube pod logs for the time window in the snippet and the exact SDK version (npm/yarn lock).
- If you can produce a curl/minimal request that exercises the large document set, paste it into the HubSpot deal notes (link below).

I’ve attached the postcall-checklist.pdf with the reproducible checks we’ll run. After we reproduce, plan is: reproduce -> isolate (structured_output toggle / token guard) -> deploy targeted patch (if needed).

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ATLAS-437

See you Fri.
